# ARC

1. On an autumn afternoon at the Limmat below the Grossmünster, Emma and Noah play "Wo ist Pico?" with Grosspapi Hans's talking parrot, who always calls back "Hier ist Pico!", but Papa Daniel, busy telling a joke, forgets to latch the cage; when the crew of a real pirate ship anchored in the middle of the river shouts "Ahoi!", Pico flies out to answer them, and Kapitän Knurrbart, whose ship has never had a parrot, shuts him in the dark hold.
2. Therefore Mama Sarah buckles life jackets on the children and checks each buckle twice, Hans rows them out in his small wooden boat and tells them to climb hand over hand, and Knurrbart, who wants them to see that the parrot is his now, throws down his rope ladder, shouts his name across the water and lets only the two children up, no grown-ups on his deck; but as soon as they have told him their names he plants himself on the big hatch with the only key and laughs that at the six o'clock bell his ship sails downstream, with Pico and with anyone still aboard.
3. Noah hears Pico shouting "Ahoi!" back at the working crew from under a narrow air hatch by the mast, above the apple sacks, and tries to squeeze through, but his shoulders stick, and Emma, the only one who fits, cries that it is too dark down there, just as the Grossmünster bell begins to strike six and Knurrbart turns away to roar for the anchor.
4. Then Noah remembers the game and promises to keep talking the whole time, so Emma slides down onto the apple sacks, calls "Wo ist Pico?" into the dark and follows each "Hier ist Pico!" until Pico climbs onto her arm, and she carries him into the light under the hatch, where he sees the sky and flies out over the rail to Hans, who is rowing after the moving ship, while Knurrbart springs from the big hatch and grabs too late; Noah pulls Emma up, the ship runs with the current until it must stop at the Münsterbrücke, and Knurrbart, who wanted a parrot and not passengers, has the crew set the children down the ladder into Hans's boat and stamps on his empty deck. Pico lands on Emma's shoulder and says "Danke, Emma!", and Emma is proud.
